title: Filtered colimits of flat module sheaves are flat
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site small in a coefficient universe $w$, let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on it, and let $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ denote sheaves of $R$-modules with section groups in $w$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $I$ be a $w$-small nonempty directed poset (any two elements have a common upper bound), and let $(P_i,p_{ij})_{i\le j}$ be a diagram in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Suppose every $P_i$ is flat, meaning that the sheaf tensor functor $P_i\otimes_R-$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If $q_i:P_i\to P$ is any colimit cocone in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], then $P$ is flat. In particular, for every finite diagram $D$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, the canonical comparison
$$P\otimes_R\lim D\ \longrightarrow\ \lim(P\otimes_R D)$$
is an isomorphism, including when $D$ is empty. No sectionwise-flatness or enough-points hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: A nonempty directed poset I is filtered. Module sheaves have coefficient-small colimits and finite limits. The underlying abelian-sheaf functor toSheaf preserves these colimits, preserves and reflects finite limits. Abelian sheaves have exact filtered colimits by exact sheafification and the corresponding property of abelian groups. Apply Mathlib HasExactColimitsOfShape.domain_of_functor to toSheaf to obtain HasExactColimitsOfShape I Mod(R). Its general preservesFiniteLimits member, recorded in the Mathlib match of lem-sfb-grothendieck-filtered-finite-limits, gives left exactness of colim_I. No generator or K-injective resolution is needed, and the site need only be essentially small in the coefficient universe.

proof.text: For each i, flatness gives finite-limit preservation of siteSheafTensorRight (F_i). The comparison siteSheafTensorRightIso from lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits identifies it with monoidal tensorRight (F_i). The symmetry already supplied by the tensor construction identifies tensorRight (F_i) with tensorLeft (F_i). Thus every functor tensorLeft (F_i) preserves finite limits.

proof.text: Consider the existing curriedTensor : Mod(R) -> Fun(Mod(R), Mod(R)). Evaluation at M is tensorRight M. By lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits and symmetry, this evaluation preserves the colimit of F. Mathlib preservesColimit_of_evaluation therefore shows curriedTensor preserves this colimit. The unique isomorphism from the specified arbitrary cocone tip c.pt to colimit F, followed by preservesColimitIso and colimitIsoFlipCompColim, identifies tensorLeft c.pt with (F followed by curriedTensor).flip followed by colim.

source.place: Tag 03EU, lemma-colimits-flat, part (2), using Tag 03EP, part (2).

proof.text: Mathlib preservesFiniteLimits_of_evaluation applied to (F followed by curriedTensor).flip gives finite-limit preservation, since its evaluations are tensorLeft (F_i). Compose this functor with the finite-limit-preserving colim_I from Step 1. Transport preservation through the natural isomorphism of Step 3. This proves PreservesFiniteLimits (tensorLeft c.pt), including terminal-object preservation, without any choice of new tensor or colimit structure.

source.place: Tag 03EU, lemma-colimits-flat, part (2), using Tag 03EP, part (2).

proof.text: Symmetry transports finite-limit preservation to tensorRight c.pt, and siteSheafTensorRightIso transports it to siteSheafTensorRight c.pt. Finite-colimit preservation follows from coefficient-sized tensor colimit preservation, shrunk to finite diagrams and the same comparison. Their conjunction is exactly IsFlatOnSite c.pt. Finally Mathlib preservation of limits makes the canonical limit.post D (tensorLeft c.pt) invertible for every finite category K, in any universe. This includes empty K because PreservesFiniteLimits includes the terminal object; no separate nonemptiness argument is used.
